title: a stranger's ready pull request from a fork's claude/<issue> keeps that claim from ever being released
status: fixed after 0.4.1: a pull request from a fork is no claim's, whatever its branch is called (board.claim_of; DESIGN.md, 13)

steps.note: sam, who may not write, opens a pull request marked ready from a fork, from a branch named claude/1 there, changing the file a's claim lists
the board lists a's claim with its own draft, #100, and sam's pull request as one of its own, which meets the claim on src/1.py and, marked ready, lands first

a's claim has had no commit for 25 hours and its own pull request is a draft, so the coordinator releases it and the board renames the branch, which closes #100 and leaves sam's open, as the fork's branch is another; sam's pull request hears it is idle, as any other would. Until the fix sam's ready pull request, read as the claim's, kept the claim from ever being released (G3), and each part of the fix has a mutant that breaks it here or in the search "a stranger's pull request from a fork on a due claim"
main moves past sam's branch, and the run tells sam's pull request so, as it tells any other (F17's review: nothing had held a fork's pull request to the word)
